hypothesis: Current hybrid pipeline provides the reference benchmark against which all modifications are evaluated.
required_metrics: Recall@5, Recall@10, Hit Rate@5, Hit Rate@10, MRR@10, nDCG@10, Latency
expected_trade_offs: Baseline latency (143ms p50) and baseline recall (0.5333)

hypothesis: Removing generic SymSpell spell-correction will prevent corruption of drug brand names and chemical terms; increasing BM25 keyword recall.
variable_changed: Replace SymSpell normalize_text with medical regex tokenizer (hyphen-preserving lowercase subword preservation)
fixed_controls: FAISS index + RRF (k=60) + Cross-Encoder pool (15) + cutoff (5)
required_metrics: BM25 Recall@10, BM25 MRR@10, Hybrid Recall@5
expected_trade_offs: Startup BM25 indexing time slightly faster; no spelling correction for true user typos
rollback_condition: BM25 Recall@10 on CAT-01/CAT-02 drops by > 0.02

experiment_name: Expand BM25 Searchable Fields & Index Drug_Dict
hypothesis: Adding warnings; adverse reactions; dosage; and drug_dict into searchable text will capture indication and safety queries missed by current title-only fields.
variable_changed: Expand extract_text_for_bm25 to include warnings_and_cautions; adverse_reactions; dosage; and query drug_dict in text mode
expected_trade_offs: Average document length increases; slight increase in BM25 scoring latency (~15ms)
rollback_condition: BM25 latency exceeds 250ms p50 or Precision@5 drops by > 0.05

hypothesis: Expanding dense FAISS candidate pool from 15 to 30 will surface relevant semantic documents that are currently truncated before RRF fusion.
required_metrics: Dense Recall@30, RRF Recall@10, Hybrid Recall@5
expected_trade_offs: FAISS search time negligible increase (+2ms); RRF candidate pool increases from 30 to 45
rollback_condition: Hybrid Recall@5 does not improve while total latency increases > 50ms

experiment_name: RRF Rank Constant & Dynamic Channel Weighting
hypothesis: Tuning RRF constant k from 60 to 20 and weighting BM25 higher (1.5x) for brand lookups will ensure exact keyword hits are not suppressed by dense scores.
variable_changed: RRF constant k (20 vs 60 vs 100) and channel weight ratio (Dense:BM25)
required_metrics: RRF MRR@10, RRF Recall@10, CAT-01 MRR
expected_trade_offs: Parameter sensitivity; potential slight drop in purely conceptual symptom queries
rollback_condition: Macro MRR@10 on Dev split declines relative to baseline k=60

hypothesis: Expanding CE pool to 30 maximizes reranker coverage; applying a calibrated score threshold (logit >= -0.5) will reject negative controls and eliminate false positives.
variable_changed: Cross-Encoder input candidate pool (15 -> 30) and dynamic logit threshold (tau >= -0.5)
required_metrics: Hybrid Recall@5, nDCG@10, Rejection Accuracy@5, Latency p95
expected_trade_offs: CPU inference latency increases from ~180ms to ~350ms per query
rollback_condition: Latency p95 exceeds 1500ms or Rejection Accuracy fails to exceed 80%

hypothesis: Expanding lay symptom queries (e.g. 'headache' -> 'cephalalgia migraine tension headache') will improve dense and sparse retrieval across varied terminology.
variable_changed: Add rule-based clinical synonym expansion for CAT-05 (symptom) and CAT-07 (multi-symptom)
required_metrics: CAT-05 Recall@5; CAT-07 Recall@5; Overall Recall@5
expected_trade_offs: Potential semantic drift or query bloat if expansion terms are overly broad
rollback_condition: Precision@5 on CAT-05 drops by > 0.08 due to semantic drift

hypothesis: Routing queries by detected intent (suppressing disease index for brand lookups; suppressing prescription drugs for lay symptoms) will eliminate context dilution.
variable_changed: Upstream intent classifier routes query to target indexes (CAT-01/02/03 -> drugs; CAT-05/07 -> diseases; CAT-12 -> emergency)
fixed_controls: Retriever algorithms fixed; only index targets filtered
expected_trade_offs: Misclassification could route a hybrid query to the wrong single index; requires fallback
rollback_condition: Classification error rate on Dev split > 5% or Recall drops on multi-intent cases

hypothesis: Comparing general-domain all-MiniLM-L6-v2 against biomedical embeddings (bge-small-en-v1.5; S-PubMedBert-MS-MARCO) will improve clinical semantic retrieval.
required_metrics: Dense Recall@10, Dense MRR@10, Hybrid Recall@5
expected_trade_offs: Requires index re-embedding and FAISS rebuilding; increased memory footprint
rollback_condition: Dense Recall@10 fails to exceed all-MiniLM-L6-v2 by at least +0.03

hypothesis: Replacing ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 with bge-reranker-base or BioLinkBERT will enhance clinical relevance discrimination and handle longer context windows.
expected_trade_offs: Larger model size; slower CPU inference (may require quantization or GPU)
rollback_condition: Reranker inference latency exceeds 800ms p50 without >= +0.05 nDCG gain
